    r = client.post(f"/admin/entries/{entry_id}/override", data={"decision": "approved", "csrf_token": token, "caption": ""})
    assert r.status_code == 400
    assert "A caption of 1-12 words is needed" in r.text


def test_override_approve_captionless_pending_entry_with_caption_succeeds(client, test_db):
    """12. Approve caption-less pending entry with a valid caption -> 303, updates DB and /result/{public_id}."""
    with test_db() as s:
        entry = Entry(
            name="Neha Shah",
            city="Surat",
            contact="neha@example.com",
            contact_type="email",
            story="Quiet chai at my desk mock-error",
            consent=True,
            consent_at=utcnow(),
            status="pending_review",
            ai_decision=None,
            ai_caption=None,
        )
        s.add(entry)
        s.commit()
        entry_id = entry.id
        public_id = entry.public_id

    client.post("/admin/login", data={"username": "test-admin", "password": "test-pass"})
    token = get_csrf_token(client)

    r = client.post(
        f"/admin/entries/{entry_id}/override",
        data={"decision": "approved", "csrf_token": token, "caption": "Quiet chai, loud thoughts"},
    )
    assert r.status_code == 303

    with test_db() as s:
        updated = s.get(Entry, entry_id)
        assert updated.status == "approved"
        assert updated.admin_override is True
        assert updated.ai_decision is None
        assert updated.ai_caption == "Quiet chai, loud thoughts"

    # Public page shows the caption
    result_page = client.get(f"/result/{public_id}")
    assert result_page.status_code == 200
    assert "Quiet chai, loud thoughts" in result_page.text


def test_override_reject_approved_entry(client, test_db):
    """13. Reject an approved entry -> 303, /result no longer shows caption, ai_decision is unchanged."""
    with test_db() as s:
        entry = Entry(
            name="Rohan Verma",
            city="Mumbai",
            contact="rohan@example.com",
            contact_type="email",
            story="Morning cutting chai by Marine Drive.",
            consent=True,
            consent_at=utcnow(),
            status="approved",
            ai_decision="approved",
            ai_caption="Marine Drive chai magic",
        )
        s.add(entry)
        s.commit()
        entry_id = entry.id
        public_id = entry.public_id

    client.post("/admin/login", data={"username": "test-admin", "password": "test-pass"})
    token = get_csrf_token(client)

    r = client.post(
        f"/admin/entries/{entry_id}/override",
        data={"decision": "rejected", "csrf_token": token},
    )
    assert r.status_code == 303

    with test_db() as s:
        updated = s.get(Entry, entry_id)
        assert updated.status == "rejected"
        assert updated.admin_override is True
        assert updated.ai_decision == "approved"  # preserved!

    # Result page no longer shows the caption publicly
    result_page = client.get(f"/result/{public_id}")
    assert result_page.status_code == 200
    assert "Marine Drive chai magic" not in result_page.text


def test_override_open_redirect_prevented(client, test_db):
    """14. back=https://evil.example redirects safely to /admin?status=all."""
    with test_db() as s:
        entry = Entry(
            name="Asha Rao",
            city="Pune",
            contact="asha@example.com",
            contact_type="email",
            story="Evening chai with family.",
            consent=True,
            consent_at=utcnow(),
            status="approved",
            ai_caption="Family chai warmth",
        )
        s.add(entry)
        s.commit()
        entry_id = entry.id

    client.post("/admin/login", data={"username": "test-admin", "password": "test-pass"})
    token = get_csrf_token(client)

    r = client.post(
        f"/admin/entries/{entry_id}/override",
        data={"decision": "rejected", "csrf_token": token, "back": "https://evil.example"},
    )
    assert r.status_code == 303
    assert r.headers.get("location") == "/admin?status=all"


def test_override_approve_ai_rejected_entry_requires_fresh_caption(client, test_db):
    """Bonus (open decision): Overriding an AI-rejected entry to approved requires a typed caption."""
    with test_db() as s:
        entry = Entry(
            name="Spam Bot",
            city="Goa",
            contact="spambot@example.com",
            contact_type="email",
            story="Buy cheap watches now at http://x.example chai",
            consent=True,
            consent_at=utcnow(),
            status="rejected",
            ai_decision="rejected",
            ai_caption="Not a chai break story",
        )
        s.add(entry)
        s.commit()
        entry_id = entry.id

    client.post("/admin/login", data={"username": "test-admin", "password": "test-pass"})
    token = get_csrf_token(client)

    # Approving without caption fails
    r1 = client.post(
        f"/admin/entries/{entry_id}/override",
        data={"decision": "approved", "csrf_token": token, "caption": ""},
    )
    assert r1.status_code == 400

    # Approving with caption succeeds and overwrites the rejection caption
    r2 = client.post(
        f"/admin/entries/{entry_id}/override",
        data={"decision": "approved", "csrf_token": token, "caption": "Overridden genuine tea moment"},
    )
    assert r2.status_code == 303

    with test_db() as s:
        updated = s.get(Entry, entry_id)
        assert updated.status == "approved"
        assert updated.ai_caption == "Overridden genuine tea moment"
        assert updated.admin_override is True


# ==============================================================================
# D. Dashboard
# ==============================================================================


def test_dashboard_status_filter(client, test_db):
    """15. Filter pending_review / approved / rejected / bogus lists only matching entries."""
    with test_db() as s:
        s.add_all([
            Entry(name="PendingAsha", city="Pune", contact="a@a.com", contact_type="email", story="Story 1", consent=True, consent_at=utcnow(), status="pending_review"),
            Entry(name="ApprovedRavi", city="Delhi", contact="b@b.com", contact_type="email", story="Story 2", consent=True, consent_at=utcnow(), status="approved", ai_caption="Cap 2"),
            Entry(name="RejectedSpam", city="Goa", contact="c@c.com", contact_type="email", story="Story 3", consent=True, consent_at=utcnow(), status="rejected", ai_reason="Spam"),
        ])
        s.commit()

    client.post("/admin/login", data={"username": "test-admin", "password": "test-pass"})

    # All
    r_all = client.get("/admin", params={"status": "all"})
    assert "PendingAsha" in r_all.text and "ApprovedRavi" in r_all.text and "RejectedSpam" in r_all.text

    # Approved only
    r_app = client.get("/admin", params={"status": "approved"})
    assert "ApprovedRavi" in r_app.text
    assert "PendingAsha" not in r_app.text
    assert "RejectedSpam" not in r_app.text

    # Rejected only
    r_rej = client.get("/admin", params={"status": "rejected"})
    assert "RejectedSpam" in r_rej.text
    assert "ApprovedRavi" not in r_rej.text
    assert "PendingAsha" not in r_rej.text

    # Pending only
    r_pen = client.get("/admin", params={"status": "pending_review"})
    assert "PendingAsha" in r_pen.text
    assert "ApprovedRavi" not in r_pen.text
    assert "RejectedSpam" not in r_pen.text

    # Bogus falls back to all
    r_bogus = client.get("/admin", params={"status": "bogus"})
    assert "PendingAsha" in r_bogus.text and "ApprovedRavi" in r_bogus.text and "RejectedSpam" in r_bogus.text


def test_dashboard_xss_escaping(client, test_db):
    """16. A story containing <script>alert(1)</script> is escaped in dashboard HTML."""
    with test_db() as s:
        entry = Entry(
            name="Tom Lee",
            city="Agra",
            contact="tom@example.com",
            contact_type="email",
            story="<script>alert(1)</script> chai with family",
            consent=True,
            consent_at=utcnow(),
            status="approved",
            ai_caption="Family chai",
        )
        s.add(entry)
        s.commit()

    client.post("/admin/login", data={"username": "test-admin", "password": "test-pass"})
    r = client.get("/admin")
    assert "<script>alert(1)</script>" not in r.text
    assert "<script>alert(1)</script>" in r.text

    """8. Cookie signed with a different secret or tampered value -> 303 to /admin/login."""
    from itsdangerous import URLSafeTimedSerializer

    # 1. Real cookie signed with a completely different secret key

- **Rejected Suggestions:**
  - Rejected `httpx2 dependency` recommendation (unnecessary third-party library; standard library and existing `httpx` dependencies were used instead).

---

## Directives & Step-by-Step Architecture

### Step 1: Security Primitives (`app/security.py`)
- Constant-time credential checking using `hmac.compare_digest` on UTF-8 bytes to prevent timing attacks.
- In-memory `LoginLimiter` tracking failed attempts per IP address using a deque sliding window (max 5 failures per 900 seconds), returning `429 Too Many Requests`.
- Constant-time `csrf_ok` token validation preventing CSRF attacks.

### Step 2: Session & Authentication Guard (`app/admin.py`)
- Integrated Starlette `SessionMiddleware` using HMAC-SHA256 signing with `SECRET_KEY`, `HttpOnly=True`, `SameSite="lax"`, and configurable `COOKIE_SECURE`.
- Attached the `require_admin` dependency guard to the protected admin router so subsequent admin endpoints inherit protection automatically.
- Generated cryptographically random CSRF tokens upon login stored in the signed session.

### Step 3: Admin Moderation Dashboard (`app/admin.py` & `app/templates/admin_dashboard.html`)
- Moderation dashboard listing all entries with filter links (`all`, `pending_review`, `approved`, `rejected`), strictly defaulting invalid filters to `"all"`.
- Paginated table showing full details (name, city, contact, full story, AI decision, reason, category, error) behind admin authentication.

### Step 4: Admin Override & Open Decisions

# Kadak Chai Co. — #MyChaiBreak

Production-grade FastAPI application for the Kadak Chai Co. (#MyChaiBreak) campaign. The platform accepts user-submitted chai break stories, executes automated AI content moderation and category classification, publishes approved stories to a public wall, and provides a protected administrative moderation dashboard with CSRF-guarded overrides.

---

## Architecture & System Overview

The system is constructed with FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0, Pydantic v2, and Jinja2 templates. It operates around three core workflows:

1. **Public Submission & Verification (`/`, `/submit`, `/result/{public_id}`):** Users submit chai stories with strict input validation, contact normalization, and consent verification. Submissions are processed through the AI pipeline, persisted to SQLite, and redirected via Post/Redirect/Get (PRG) to a bookmarkable result page.
2. **Automated AI Moderation Pipeline (`app/ai/`):** Evaluates stories for brand fit and safety, assigning an approved or rejected decision, a category (`funny`, `nostalgic`, `wholesome`, `other`), and a 1–12 word caption. Any AI or network failure automatically falls back to `pending_review`.
3. **Protected Admin Management (`/admin`):** Secure dashboard for campaign moderators to inspect submissions, filter by status, and override decisions with CSRF-protected forms.

---

## Privacy & Security Architecture

### Zero-Leak Public Privacy Design
- **Public Feed Disclosure:** The public story wall (`/`) and public shareable result cards (`/result/{public_id}`) expose **only** the submitter's first name (`name.split()[0]`) and the approved 1–12 word caption.
- **Identifier Decoupling:** Submissions use an internal sequential integer primary key (`id`) for database indexing and a cryptographically random 22-character URL-safe string (`public_id`) generated via `secrets.token_urlsafe(16)` for public routing. Public endpoints reject internal numeric IDs with `404 Not Found`.
- **Confidential Field Protection:** Submitter contact information (email/phone), submitter city, full story text, and internal moderation diagnostics (`ai_error`, `ai_reason`) are never rendered in public HTML templates or transmitted to unauthenticated clients.

### Traceback & Logging Sanitization
- All AI client calls and external integrations use `raise ... from None` to sever Python exception chains. Sensitive Groq/OpenAI API keys, HTTP request headers, raw response bodies, and submitter story contents are strictly prevented from appearing in server logs or traceback outputs.

### Admin Security & Access Control
- **Signed Session Authentication:** Admin sessions are managed via Starlette `SessionMiddleware` using HMAC-SHA256 cookie signing (`SECRET_KEY`), configured with `HttpOnly=True`, `SameSite="lax"`, and configurable `COOKIE_SECURE` (enforced HTTPS in production).
- **Timing-Safe Credential Verification:** `check_credentials()` evaluates username and password using `hmac.compare_digest` on encoded bytes, eliminating timing side-channel attacks.
- **Brute-Force Rate Limiting:** An in-memory sliding-window `LoginLimiter` monitors failed authentication attempts per client IP address. Exceeding 5 failures within a 900-second window blocks subsequent attempts with `429 Too Many Requests`.
- **CSRF-Protected Overrides:** All admin override state changes are submitted via `POST` with a session-matched CSRF token verified via constant-time byte comparison (`csrf_ok`).
- **AI-Rejected Override Policy:** Approving an entry previously rejected by AI (or an entry without an existing caption) mandates a fresh 1–12 word admin caption. This prevents automated rejection notes (e.g., explaining why a post is unsuitable) from publishing to the public feed.
- **Open-Redirect Protection:** The post-override `back` redirect parameter is strictly validated against recognized filter keys (`all`, `pending_review`, `approved`, `rejected`), defaulting to `/admin?status=all` if any untrusted or external URL is supplied.

---

## AI Moderation Pipeline

The moderation engine supports two distinct execution providers configured via `AI_PROVIDER`:

1. **Deterministic Mock Provider (`mock`):** Used for deterministic testing and local offline development. Evaluates input text for explicit test triggers (e.g., `"coffee"`, `"badword"`, `"chai mock-broken"`) to generate predictable `approved`, `rejected`, or simulated failure states.
2. **Live LLM Provider (`groq`):** Connects to Groq's OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoint using `openai/gpt-oss-20b`.
   - **Token Allocation:** Configured with `max_tokens=500` to allocate sufficient space for the model's internal reasoning tokens (~166 tokens) before generating response JSON.
   - **Schema Compliance:** Outputs JSON matching `AIResult` (`decision`, `reason`, `category`, `caption`). Markdown fences and formatting artifacts are stripped and validated by Pydantic v2 in `app/ai/parse.py`.
   - **Fail-Safe Fallback:** If the provider is unreachable, times out, or emits unparseable JSON, `analyze_story` traps the exception and returns `status="pending_review"` with `ai_decision="rejected"` and a sanitized error code (`api_down`, `timeout`, `invalid_json`, `schema_error`).

---

## Local Setup & Installation

### 1. Clone & Environment Setup

```bash
git clone <repository-url>
cd kadak_chai

# Create and activate virtual environment
python -m venv .venv

# On Linux/macOS:
source .venv/bin/activate

# On Windows:
.venv\Scripts\activate

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### 2. Environment Configuration

Create a `.env` file in the project root based on `.env.example`:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

| Variable | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SECRET_KEY` | Yes | *None* | 32+ character random string for signing session cookies. |
| `ADMIN_USERNAME` | Yes | *None* | Username for admin dashboard authentication. |
| `ADMIN_PASSWORD` | Yes | *None* | Password for admin dashboard authentication. |
| `AI_PROVIDER` | Yes | `mock` | Moderation provider (`mock` or `groq`). Unrecognized values fail loud on startup. |
| `AI_API_KEY` | Conditional | `""` | Groq API key (required if `AI_PROVIDER=groq`). |
| `AI_BASE_URL` | No | `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` | Base URL for OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint. |
| `AI_MODEL` | No | `openai/gpt-oss-20b` | Model identifier on the LLM endpoint. |
| `DATABASE_URL` | No | `sqlite:///./kadak.db` | SQLAlchemy database connection string. |
| `COOKIE_SECURE` | No | `false` | Set to `true` in production to enforce `Secure` HTTPS cookies. |

Generate a cryptographically secure `SECRET_KEY`:
```bash
python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"
```

### 3. Running the Server

```bash
uvicorn app.main:app --reload
```

The application will be accessible at `http://127.0.0.1:8000`:
- **Landing Page & Submission Form:** `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`
- **Admin Dashboard:** `http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin`

# AI Usage, Engineering Ownership & Audit Trail

This document details the engineering methodology, session history, model attribution, and explicit authorship boundaries across the development of the Kadak Chai Co. (#MyChaiBreak) repository.

---

## 1. Tools & Models Reference Table

The development workflow spanned four distinct AI-assisted sessions (`S1` through `S4`), tracked in `AI_SESSIONS.json`:

| Session | Tool | Model | Date | Verified Commits | Primary Scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **S1** | Claude (web) | Claude (web) | 2026-11-17 | `b4129a8`, `28d27f5`, `a48078a`, `0a1a478`, `6a0841a`, `8811821`, `272f7d3` | Architecture design, data models, configuration with loud failure, mock AI provider, and OpenAI-compatible Groq client. |
| **S2** | Antigravity | `gemini-3.8-flash-high (Antigravity)` | 2026-11-17 | `bdb40e8` | Public submission flow, Jinja2 templates, chai-themed CSS styling, Post/Redirect/Get pattern, outcome cards, and public route integration tests. |
| **S3** | Gemini (web) | Gemini (web) | 2026-11-17 | `833cfa6`, `823100c`, `727dc77`, `c135a4a`, `d637bce` | Orchestrator logic with safe `pending_review` fallback, 69-test TDD validation specification, live Groq testing, and 300-char story limit enforcement. |
| **S4** | Claude (web) | Claude (web) | 2026-11-18 | `8ca160b`, `1578585`, `3b3d4bd`, `ca7f4c5`, `1c693b0`, `6a4f26a`, `d5a36c7`, `949a0c4` | Admin authentication, sliding-window rate limiting, signed session cookies, admin dashboard, CSRF-protected override workflow, and admin test suite. |

---

## 2. Precise Authorship & Hand-Written Attribution

To guarantee architectural integrity, security, and exact specification compliance, all critical validation algorithms and security-sensitive test harnesses were written entirely by hand rather than generated:

### Hand-Written Components
1. **`app/ai/parse.py`:** Written entirely by hand. Implements strict JSON extraction, markdown code block stripping, boundary sanitization, and Pydantic validation without relying on LLM-generated parsing shortcuts.
2. **`tests/test_parse.py`:** Written entirely by hand. Comprises 30 unit tests covering edge cases, truncated JSON payloads, nested markdown fences, and schema failures.
3. **`app/validation.py`:** Written entirely by hand. Implements `normalise_contact()`, `_collapse_spaces()`, and `validate_submission()` against the 69-test TDD test specification generated in `S3`. Handles multi-field error accumulation (`HTTP 422`), email regex, phone formatting/normalization, and the 300-character story limit.
4. **`tests/test_security.py`:** Written entirely by hand. Comprises 14 unit tests covering constant-time credential verification, non-ASCII byte handling, sliding-window limiter lockout, fake clock expiration, reset operations, and constant-time CSRF token comparison.
5. **`tests/test_admin.py`:** Written entirely by hand. Comprises 16 comprehensive access-control and override tests covering route introspection, credential authentication, rate limiter lockout, session lifecycle, tampered session cookies (including real wrong-secret `itsdangerous.URLSafeTimedSerializer` cookies), CSRF token validation, open-redirect prevention, and AI-rejected caption requirements.

### AI-Assisted & Generated Components
- **`tests/test_validation.py`:** Generated in `S3` as a 69-test TDD specification suite prior to the hand-written implementation of `app/validation.py`.
- **Scaffolded Application Code:** Initial FastAPI app lifespan, database engine setup (`app/db.py`), `Entry` model (`app/models.py`), mock AI provider (`app/ai/mock.py`), and Groq client skeleton (`app/ai/client.py`) scaffolded in `S1`.
- **Frontend Templates & Styling:** `app/static/style.css`, `app/templates/base.html`, `index.html`, and `result.html` generated in `S2`.
- **Admin Modules:** `app/security.py`, `app/admin.py`, and admin templates scaffolded in `S4`.

---

## 3. Verbatim Prompts & Review Directives

### A. Verbatim `S2` Public Flow Prompt (Extracted from Local History)

The following prompt was submitted to Antigravity (`gemini-3.8-flash-high`) on 2026-11-17 to execute Phase 3 public submission flow (`bdb40e8`):

```text
We are completing Phase 3 (Public Submission Flow) of the "Kadak Chai Co." (#MyChaiBreak) FastAPI + SQLAlchemy + Jinja2 app.

First, read `requirements.txt`, `app/main.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/models.py`, `app/validation.py`, and `app/ai/__init__.py` so every import, column name, and dependency matches the existing codebase exactly. (If `jinja2` or `python-multipart` is missing from `requirements.txt`, add them and install into `.venv`.)

Do NOT modify `app/validation.py`, `app/models.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/ai/*`, `tests/test_ai.py`, `tests/test_parse.py`, or `tests/test_validation.py`.

Build the following cleanly:

1. **Templates & Styling (`app/templates/` and `app/static/`):**
   - `app/static/style.css`: Warm, high-contrast "Kadak Chai Co." editorial styling (cream/parchment background, deep chai-brown & terracotta accents, clean typography, responsive card layout, accessible form focus states, clear status badges for `approved`, `rejected`, and `pending_review`, and mobile-friendly spacing).
   - `app/templates/base.html`: Shared HTML5 layout linking `/static/style.css`, campaign header ("Kadak Chai Co. — #MyChaiBreak"), and clean footer. Jinja2 auto-escaping must stay enabled everywhere (never use `| safe` on user input).
   - `app/templates/index.html`:
     - Campaign hero + rules summary + story submission form (`POST /submit`) with fields: `name`, `city`, `contact` (email or phone), `story` (with live JS character counter `0 / 2000`, purely progressive enhancement—server validation remains authoritative), and `consent` checkbox.
     - Displays field-level errors (`errors.get(...)`) next to each invalid field and preserves previously entered form values (`form_data`) on HTTP 422 validation errors.
     - Displays a curated "Approved #MyChaiBreak Stories" wall below the form showing only `status == "approved"` entries (displaying `ai_caption`, `story`, `name`, and `city` — NEVER exposing `contact`, `id`, `ai_error`, or non-approved entries).
   - `app/templates/result.html`:
     - Displays the submission outcome for `/result/{public_id}`:
       - `approved`: Celebratory card with the AI-generated `ai_caption`, category badge (`ai_category`), submitter name/city, and their story.
       - `rejected`: Polite card showing `ai_reason` explaining why the story didn't qualify for the campaign wall, plus a link to submit another story.
       - `pending_review`: Reassuring card explaining the story is queued for human review (NEVER leaking `ai_error` codes or internal trace details to the public page).
     - Includes a shareable/bookmarkable status link notice.

2. **Public Routes in `app/main.py`:**
   - Mount `/static` using `StaticFiles` (resolve paths with `Path(__file__).resolve().parent` so tests work from any working directory) and configure `Jinja2Templates`.
   - Keep existing `lifespan` and `GET /health`.
   - `GET /`: Queries the latest approved entries (`Entry.status == "approved"`, ordered by `created_at.desc()`, limit 20) and renders `index.html`.
   - `POST /submit`:
     - Reads form fields (`name`, `city`, `contact`, `story`, `consent: str | None = Form(default=None)`).
     - Calls `validate_submission(name, city, contact, story, consent)`.
     - On `SubmissionValidationError as exc`: re-queries approved entries and renders `index.html` with `errors=exc.errors`, `form_data=...`, and `status_code=422`.
     - On valid submission: calls `outcome = analyze_story(valid.story)`, creates an `Entry` with `consent_at=utcnow()`, `status=outcome.status`, `ai_decision=outcome.ai_decision`, `ai_reason=outcome.ai_reason`, `ai_category=outcome.ai_category`, `ai_caption=outcome.ai_caption`, `ai_error=outcome.ai_error`, commits to DB, and returns `RedirectResponse(url=f"/result/{entry.public_id}", status_code=303)` (Post/Redirect/Get pattern so refreshing never double-submits).
   - `GET /result/{public_id}`:
     - Looks up `Entry` by `public_id`. If not found (or if someone passes a numeric internal `id`), returns HTTP 404.
     - Renders `result.html` with the entry.

3. **Integration Tests (`tests/test_public_routes.py`):**
   - Use an isolated in-memory or temporary SQLite database via FastAPI `dependency_overrides[get_db]` and `monkeypatch.setattr(config, "AI_PROVIDER", "mock")` so tests never touch `kadak.db` or make external network calls.
   - Test:
     - `GET /` returns 200 and renders the form and only `approved` stories (never `rejected` or `pending_review` stories, and never user `contact` info).
     - `POST /submit` with valid chai story redirects (`303`) to `/result/{public_id}`, saves `Entry` in DB, and `GET /result/{public_id}` shows the approved status + AI caption.
     - `POST /submit` with spam/off-topic story redirects (`303`) to `/result/{public_id}` and shows rejected status + reason, and does NOT appear on `GET /`.
     - `POST /submit` when AI fails (`"chai mock-broken"`) redirects (`303`) to `/result/{public_id}`, stores `status="pending_review"` and `ai_error="invalid_json"` in DB, and renders the pending message on `/result/{public_id}` WITHOUT leaking `"invalid_json"` in the HTML.
     - `POST /submit` with invalid fields returns `422` with field error messages and preserves submitted input values.
     - `GET /result/nonexistent-id` and `GET /result/1` (numeric internal ID) return `404`.
     - XSS check: submitting `<script>alert('xss')</script>` in `name` or `story` renders escaped HTML (`<script>`) on both `/` and `/result/{public_id}`.

Run `pytest -v` after creating these files and report the results.
```

---

### B. Verbatim `S4` Review Directives & Open Decision Specifications

The following review directives and architectural constraints were established during the `S4` session:

1. **Security & Rate Limiting Directives (`app/security.py`):**
   - Use `hmac.compare_digest` with encoded bytes for username and password comparison.
   - Enforce an in-memory sliding-window limiter with an injectable monotonic clock: max 5 failures per 900-second window per IP.
2. **Session Cookie Directives (`app/admin.py`):**
   - Attach Starlette `SessionMiddleware` using `SECRET_KEY`, `HttpOnly=True`, and `SameSite="lax"`.
   - Guard all protected admin routes using a router-level dependency (`require_admin`).
3. **Override CSRF & Caption Decision:**
   - Overriding an entry via `POST /admin/entries/{entry_id}/override` requires a constant-time validated CSRF token matching the session.
   - **Open Decision Rule:** When overriding an AI-rejected entry (or an entry without an existing caption) to `approved`, the admin must type a fresh 1–12 word caption. The system rejects captionless approvals with HTTP 400. This guarantees that automated rejection reasoning is never published to the public wall.
4. **Deliberate Sabotage Verification:**
   - Temporarily comment out `csrf_ok` in `override()` and execute the test suite to verify that Test 9 fails (`400 == 403`), proving the test harness catches missing CSRF protection.

---

### C. Verbatim Orchestration Prompt (Final Audit & Documentation Verification)

The prompt driving this documentation pass, Test 8 upgrade, and secrets audit:

```text
Complete Step 2 (test upgrade, local log extraction, secrets scan) and Step 3 (documentation generation) for the Kadak Chai Co. (#MyChaiBreak) repository in one pass. Do NOT modify any frontend templates, CSS, or application runtime code yet (the S5 SVG/CSS polish pass happens after Render deployment).

Execute these 5 tasks in order:

### Task 1: Upgrade Test 8 in `tests/test_admin.py`
In `tests/test_admin.py`, update `test_tampered_or_invalid_secret_session_cookie_redirects_303` so it tests BOTH:
1. A real `itsdangerous.URLSafeTimedSerializer("a-completely-different-secret-key").dumps({"user": "test-admin"})` cookie signed with the wrong secret.
2. The `"tampered-invalid-signature-cookie"` string.
Assert both return `303` with `Location: /admin/login`. Run `pytest -q` and confirm `149 passed`.

### Task 2: Populate `ai-logs/` with Real Local Logs & Available Context
Create `ai-logs/` with four UTF-8 Markdown files:
- `ai-logs/S1-claude-web.md`
- `ai-logs/S2-antigravity.md`
- `ai-logs/S3-gemini.md`
- `ai-logs/S4-claude-web.md`

### Task 3: Write `AI_SESSIONS.json` in the Exact Brief Schema
Overwrite `AI_SESSIONS.json` (UTF-8, clean ASCII hyphens, zero corrupted ? characters) with exact top-level keys and values.

### Task 4: Write `README.md` and `AI_USAGE.md`
Write `README.md` and `AI_USAGE.md` in plain, factual engineering prose.

### Task 5: Run Full Secrets Scan & Final Verification
Run a Python script that scans `ai-logs/`, `AI_SESSIONS.json`, `AI_USAGE.md`, `README.md`, and full `git log --all -S` history for `"gsk_"` and the actual values of `AI_API_KEY`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, and `SECRET_KEY` from `.env`.
```

---

## 4. Complete Mistakes-Caught Table

The following table documents all defects and edge cases caught during development, matching `AI_SESSIONS.json`:

| Session | What Went Wrong | How It Was Caught & Resolved |
|---|-----------------|-----------------------------|
| **S1** | Spec let exception chains carry story text into tracebacks. | Architecture review; enforced `raise ... from None` across AI client calls and added traceback assertions. |
| **S1** | Suggested Groq Llama model IDs that returned 404. | Live API call against Groq `/models`; switched model ID to `openai/gpt-oss-20b`. |
| **S1** | `response_format json_object` returned 400 on Groq. | Live API test call; removed `response_format` and relied on prompt instructions + Pydantic parser. |
| **S1** | `max_tokens 200` truncated reasoning model JSON output. | Live test run produced `invalid_json` from parser due to ~166 internal reasoning tokens; raised `max_tokens` to 500. |
| **S2** | `index.html` claimed every entry is reviewed before publication and invented a 'limited-edition tea tins' promise. | Caught in `S4` review; corrected in commits `d5a36c7` and `949a0c4` to accurately reflect automated moderation. |
| **S3** | Story max length was set to 2,000 characters instead of the brief's 300-character limit. | Caught in review against project brief; updated to 300 characters across `app/validation.py`, `index.html`, and tests in `d637bce`. |
| **S4** | Predicted CSRF sabotage would fail tests 9 and 13/14; only test 9 failed because 13 and 14 send valid tokens. | Caught by executing deliberate sabotage test and analyzing assertion failure. |
| **S4** | Spec to walk `app.routes` found 0 routes in FastAPI 0.163.1 due to lazy `_IncludedRouter` objects. | Caught by `assert checked >= 2` failure on initial test execution; fixed by unpacking `original_router.routes`. |

In [tests/test_admin.py](file:///C:/Users/Krutik/CODING/01_Live_WebApps/kadak_chai/tests/test_admin.py#L162-L175), `test_tampered_or_invalid_secret_session_cookie_redirects_303` was updated to explicitly test **both**:

Both assert `303 See Other` with `Location: /admin/login`.

```python
def test_tampered_or_invalid_secret_session_cookie_redirects_303(client):
    """8. Cookie signed with a different secret or tampered value -> 303 to /admin/login."""
    from itsdangerous import URLSafeTimedSerializer

    # 1. Real cookie signed with a completely different secret key
    forged = URLSafeTimedSerializer("a-completely-different-secret-key").dumps({"user": "test-admin"})
    client.cookies.set("session", forged)
    r_forged = client.get("/admin")
    assert r_forged.status_code == 303
    assert r_forged.headers.get("location") == "/admin/login"

    # 2. Tampered / invalid signature string
    client.cookies.set("session", "tampered-invalid-signature-cookie")
    r_tampered = client.get("/admin")
    assert r_tampered.status_code == 303
    assert r_tampered.headers.get("location") == "/admin/login"
```

# S1 — Claude (web) Session Log

> **Notice:** [OPTIONAL: paste full browser export here if needed]

## Session Metadata
- **Session ID:** `S1`
- **Tool:** Claude (web)
- **Model:** Claude (web)
- **Date:** 2026-11-17
- **Goal:** Architecture planning, project initialization, core models, configuration with loud failure, deterministic mock AI, and OpenAI-compatible client for Groq.
- **Verified Commits:**
  - `b4129a8`: `chore: add gitignore and env example [S1]`
  - `28d27f5`: `chore: add dependencies and config module [S1]`
  - `a48078a`: `feat: add database setup and Entry model [S1]`
  - `0a1a478`: `feat: minimal FastAPI app with health route [S1]`
  - `6a0841a`: `feat: add AI result schema [S1]`
  - `8811821`: `feat: deterministic mock AI provider [S1]`
  - `272f7d3`: `feat: real AI provider client for Groq`
- **Files Owned / Modified:**
  - `.gitignore`
  - `.env.example`
  - `requirements.txt`
  - `app/config.py`
  - `app/db.py`
  - `app/models.py`
  - `app/main.py`
  - `app/ai/schema.py`
  - `app/ai/mock.py`
  - `app/ai/client.py`

---

## Session Overview & Key Decisions

1. **Configuration & Loud Startup Failure (`app/config.py`):**
   - Implemented strict startup validation requiring `SECRET_KEY`, `ADMIN_USERNAME`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, and `AI_PROVIDER`.
   - Prevented silent defaults that could run the app in an insecure state.

2. **Data Model Architecture (`app/models.py`):**
   - Enforced a hard separation between sequential database `id` (integer primary key) and external `public_id` (22-character random URL-safe string generated via `secrets.token_urlsafe(16)`).
   - Enforced strict separation between `ai_decision` (immutable audit record of automated moderation) and `status` (operational publication status), enabling human admin overrides without destroying audit history.
   - Enforced contact normalization fields (`contact` and `contact_type`) and explicit boolean `consent`.

3. **AI Client & Traceback Privacy (`app/ai/client.py`):**
   - Built an OpenAI-compatible HTTP client for Groq using `httpx`.
   - Enforced `raise ... from None` on all raised exceptions to sever the Python exception chain, guaranteeing that sensitive API keys, response payloads, and user stories never appear in application tracebacks or logs.

---

## Live Debugging & Mistakes Caught

| # | What Went Wrong | How It Was Caught & Resolved |
|---|-----------------|-----------------------------|
| 1 | Spec allowed exception chains to carry full story text and HTTP headers into tracebacks. | Caught during architecture review; enforced `raise ... from None` across AI client calls and verified with traceback assertions. |
| 2 | Initial suggestions included deprecated Groq Llama model IDs that returned 404. | Caught during live test call against Groq `/models` endpoint; switched default `AI_MODEL` to `openai/gpt-oss-20b`. |
| 3 | Spec suggested sending `response_format: {"type": "json_object"}`, which returned HTTP 400 on Groq for the selected model. | Caught during live API testing; removed `response_format` parameter and relied on strict system prompt instructions combined with robust Pydantic parsing. |
| 4 | Setting `max_tokens: 200` caused truncated JSON responses from `openai/gpt-oss-20b`. | Caught during live test run yielding `invalid_json` parser failures; diagnosed that the reasoning model consumes ~166 tokens for internal thought prior to emitting JSON; resolved by increasing `max_tokens` to 500. |

---

## Code Boundaries

- **Generated in S1:** Foundation files (`app/config.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/models.py`, `app/main.py` health stub, `app/ai/schema.py`, `app/ai/mock.py`, `app/ai/client.py`).
- **Written by Hand:** `app/ai/parse.py` and `tests/test_parse.py` were written by hand to ensure strict, bulletproof parsing and markdown fence extraction independent of AI code generation.

- Constant-time credential checking using `hmac.compare_digest` on UTF-8 bytes to prevent timing attacks.

### Step 2: Session & Authentication Guard (`app/admin.py`)
- Integrated Starlette `SessionMiddleware` using HMAC-SHA256 signing with `SECRET_KEY`, `HttpOnly=True`, `SameSite="lax"`, and configurable `COOKIE_SECURE`.
